images.title: Square with both diagonals
images.purpose: Show that in a square each angle between a diagonal and a side is 45 degrees and the two diagonals are equal.
images.composition: One large square centred with both diagonals; labels kept outside the square.
images.exact_structure: One square with sides of 5 cm. Both diagonals drawn, crossing at the centre, teal #0072B2, each exactly the same length, about 7.1 cm. At the bottom left corner the angle between the diagonal and the bottom side is shaded amber #E69F00 and labelled 45 degrees. Exactly 1 square, 2 diagonals, 1 shaded angle.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A square has 45 degree angles at its diagonals and two equal diagonals.
images.description: A 5 cm square with both diagonals in teal, each about 7.1 cm, and one 45 degree angle shaded in amber at a corner.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the shaded angle and say that every such angle is the same.

image_decisions.why: One square with its diagonals gives both facts.
